name: Kelly O’Shanassy
bio: Kelly absolutely loves nature, with wombats, towering gums and tranquil rivers being her favourites. This love of nature drove Kelly to become a distinguished and transformative leader at the forefront of nature and climate.

Kelly was the CEO of the Australian Conservation Foundation and is experienced in executive roles in business, government and the community sector. She has been at the forefront of Australia’s most consequential nature and climate wins over the past two decades, and is trusted by environmental and political leaders, community, business and philanthropy.
She brings thought leadership, a ‘can do’ attitude, curiosity, kindness and fun to shape innovative, high-impact organisations to drive outcomes for people and nature.

name: Mark Arnold
meta: Elected Treasurer and Deputy Chair in 2026 | Appointed Director 2026
bio: Mark is a Non-Executive Director of Freshmark, Blue Knot Foundation, and Afford, and chairs the Finance, Audit and Risk Committees of Blue Knot Foundation and Freshmark. He is also Chair of Afford’s Corporate Development Committee, a member of its Asset, Audit and Risk Committee, and an Advisory Director to two early-stage financial services technology businesses.

Mark has over 30 years’ experience in global financial services, having held senior regional and global Chief Financial Officer roles with major UK banks, primarily based in London, with international experience in Hong Kong and New York. He later became a Partner at Deloitte in Australia and South Africa within the Transformation, Technology and Strategy consulting practice, advising boards and executives across financial services and other industries.

He specialises in financial reporting including budgeting, including governance, organisational change, and risk management, with a strong focus on financial stewardship, regulatory oversight, and technology-enabled transformation. Mark is a Fellow CPA (Australia) and a Graduate of the Australian Institute of Company Directors and holds a Bachelor of Accounting from the University of Canberra.

name: Jane Danziger
bio: Jane is a proven leader in driving growth and transformation through customer centricity, digital, loyalty and data & analytics. She has a strong track record of driving customer centric change in both her senior executive and Advisory roles.

Jane spent 4 years in Executive roles at Woolworths, where she led customer, brand & marketing, loyalty, digital, the call centres, privacy, Group strategy and Group transformation. Jane was also Chair of Woolworths First Nations Advisory Board, spearheading Woolworths RAP commitments and delivery.

Prior to Woolworths she spent over 20 years with the Boston Consulting Group, where her experience includes incubating and launching innovative new digital businesses, working cross functionally with large teams to develop and implement machine learning personalisation tools, launching new products and brands, identifying growth opportunities and optimising brand portfolio positioning in airline, travel and consumer facing industries.

Jane is passionate about building high performance cross functional teams. She is also passionate about increasing the representation of women in Digital. At BCG she led GAMMA, BCGs data and analytics business, in Australia and also led Gamma’s global women’s initiative. Over 10 years she shifted the dial on diversity in BCG ANZ.

Jane loves the outdoors (hiking, kayaking, skiing) and has been actively involved with the Foundation for National Parks & Wildlife for several years. Jane is also a member of Chief Executive Women (CEW).

name: Tim Jarvis AM
bio: Environmental scientist, author, adventurer and public speaker Tim Jarvis AM is committed to finding pragmatic solutions to major environmental issues related to climate change and biodiversity loss and uses his public speaking engagements, films and books to progress thinking in these areas. He has worked in the environmental field for over 30 years both in an environmental advocacy capacity as well as providing strategic and practical environmental advice to both government and corporate organisations.

Tim is well known for his historically authentic recreations of the Antarctic survival journeys of Sir Douglas Mawson and Sir Ernest Shackleton and campaigns actively for better protection of Antarctica. He is founder and leader of The Forktree Project, a native revegetation project on South Australia’s Fleurieu Peninsula, Global Ambassador and Governor of WWF, Vice President of conservation NGO Flora and Fauna and was made Australian of the Year 2024 for South Australia.

name: Natalie Kyriacou OAM
bio: Natalie is an award-winning environmentalist, presenter, and charity director on a mission to spark curiosity about the natural world. She is the author of Nature’s Last Dance: Tales of Wonder in an Age of Extinction.

Natalie was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia and the Forbes 30 Under 30 Honour for her services to wildlife and environmental conservation in 2018. She was a United Nations Environment Programme Young Champion of the Earth Finalist. She is one of LinkedIn’s 2022 ‘Top Green Voices’ and named as one of The Australian’s 2022 ‘Top Innovators’. In 2025, she was named as a Marie Claire “Women of the Year” nominee.

Natalie is the Founder and Chair of My Green World, a Board Director at Foundation for National Parks and Wildlife, a former Board Director at CARE Australia, a W20 Delegate (official G20 engagement group), a UNESCO Green Citizens Pathfinder. She sits on the XPRIZE Global Brain Trust for Biodiversity and Conservation. She is a National Ambassador for the Australian Conservation Foundation.

name: Leisa Bacon
bio: Leisa has over 25 years of strategy, marketing and partnerships experience, spanning both Corporate and Government. Leisa is passionate about the Arts, Culture and the Environment, and has just commenced as Executive Director Partnerships and Development at Creative Australia, after a decade at the ABC.

Prior to that, Leisa predominantly worked for large, global organisations at a Director level, from P&G to the Coca-Cola Company. She was ranked #1 CMO in Australia in 2020, is a fellow of The Marketing Academy and has a Degree and Masters in Business from the Queensland University of Technology. Leisa has also completed Executive studies in design thinking at Stanford, and Leading Change at Harvard, and currently sits on the Boards of the AANA and Legs on the Wall.

name: Dr Lucas Carmody
bio: Dr. Lucas Carmody is a environmental economist and sustainability leader. Lucas is committed to helping organisations better understand the ways in which they rely on health of our natural environment and the risks posed by further degradation.

As Executive Director of PwC’s Global Centre for Nature Positive Business, he has guided organisations worldwide in understanding and managing the financial and economic impacts of climate change, and of nature and biodiversity loss. Lucas has played a key role in driving the development and adoption of frameworks, standards and methodologies essential for addressing the private sector’s role in halting and reversing nature loss. This includes partnerships with leading initiatives such as the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) and the Science Based Targets Network (SBTN).
Lucas’ commitment is rooted in the view that our economic prosperity and societal well‐being depend on the sound management of natural systems that sustain all life.

name: Kinjia Munkara-Murray
bio: Kinjia Munkara-Murray is an Indigenous scientist with a strong commitment to integrating Western and First Nations knowledge systems to drive lasting environmental, biodiversity and community outcomes. She has experience across government, corporate and research contexts. She works at Melbourne Water, amplifying Indigenous-led perspectives in land and water management and statutory decision-making.

Kinjia is a Graduate of the Australian Indigenous Governance Institute’s Emerging Directors Program, and is a Non-Executive Director of Watertrust Australia. She is also an Ambassador for DeadlyScience and holds a Master of Science (Bioscience).

Kinjia has expertise in environmental policy, waterway and catchment management, and science-informed community engagement processes. She also has a particular interest in biodiversity conservation and environmental stewardship.

name: Nick Tubb
bio: Nick Tubb is Head of Financial Services & Travel for Australia and New Zealand at Meta, where over 11 years he has led strategic partnerships with major Australian organisations.

Nick has been involved with FNPW since 2020, initially as an observer and contributing through the Marketing Sub-Committee for over five years. He brings commercial insight, experience operating at scale, and a focus on measurable, data-informed strategy to support the Foundation’s mission.
